assign.outcome:
**Accept/Reject buttons landed on every row of `/framework/ai/2026-08-17/layout-primitives/`** — reuses the site's plain `button()`, no new CSS, no new component. A click writes one `{"verdict":{"id","accept","at"}}` line to `verdicts.jsonl` over the dev socket, following `ext/DesignTool/audit/twin.js:85-91` exactly (the write RPC WRITES, not appends: fetch the file as text, add a line, resend whole — comment at the top of `page.js` says so). `ext/JSONL` and `ext/Saver` were checked first per the brief; neither offers an append RPC (JSONL only replays, Saver's `FileSaver.write` pretty-prints a whole JSON doc), so twin.js's pattern was used directly. On load, latest verdict per id wins; each card shows an accepted/rejected tag, a rejected card repeats its revert line under a "to apply" label. Header reads `N accepted · N rejected · N open`.

Proof (headless, fresh context): accepted `card-frame`, rejected `muted` — header went `0 accepted · 0 rejected · 22 open` to `1 accepted · 1 rejected · 20 open`; `verdicts.jsonl` held exactly those two lines; reload kept both tags. Then rm'd the file over the socket — Mike's file is **absent**, not empty (404, matching its pre-task state); header reads `0 accepted · 0 rejected · 22 open` again.

[The screen](/framework/ai/2026-08-17/layout-primitives/) · ![proof](proof.png)

Left out: nothing — no RPC gap found, so no proposal-and-stop needed.
